uncited: The method builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](2812-3d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md) but replaces the alpha blending calculation with an exact volumetric integration.
The method uses the standard 3D Gaussian attributes defined in [3D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](2812-3d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md).
No new complex data structures are required beyond the standard Gaussian attributes and the ray parameters.
To compute the accumulated transmittance $\overline{T}_j$ across a specific Gaussian $j$, we project the 3D Gaussian onto the 1D ray.
The accumulated opacity $\alpha_i$ for the $i$-th Gaussian is derived from the transmittance entering and leaving it.
The following pseudocode implements the analytic transmittance computation for a single pixel, assuming a list of sorted Gaussians intersecting the ray.

*   **Degenerate Covariance**: If $\mathbf{d}^T \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j^{-1} \mathbf{d}$ is near zero (e.g., Gaussian is infinitely thin in the ray direction), $\beta_j$ becomes large and numerical instability may occur.
*   **Infinite Support Assumption**: The analytic formula assumes infinite support for the Gaussian integral.
*   **Time Complexity**: Similar to 3DGS rasterization, $O(N)$ per pixel where $N$ is the number of Gaussians covering the pixel.
The analytic computation adds a constant overhead per Gaussian (matrix-vector multiplications and exponentials) compared to the 2D splatting approximation.
